title: A Bakery for the Harbor
premise: Mara Voss has built a career on being nobody: the ghostwriter behind other people's stories, including the memoir of celebrated chef Elias Thorne—her ex-lover and the man whose bakery empire she once helped build before vanishing from his life. When a snowstorm traps them both in his shuttered harbor bakery on Greywater Island, old truths surface alongside flour and grief, forcing Mara to confront why she left and who she became to survive. As the storm clears, she must choose between delivering the manuscript that will erase her voice forever and claiming her own name in print—and in his kitchen. The book ends with Mara publishing under her own byline as the last ferry departs, with Elias aboard beside her.
about_author: Ulyana Halloran is a former line cook turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, harbors, and the long silences between people. She lives on a cold coast with a sourdough starter older than her marriage.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In a Manhattan office, Mara signs the contract to ghostwrite Elias Thorne's memoir, hiding her history with him from her editor. She tells herself the heart is trainable. Emotional beat: controlled dread masked as professionalism.

chapters.title: Interview One: Bread and Bitterness
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. First taped interview at Thorne's test kitchen; Elias is guarded, sharp, and clearly recognizes something familiar in her questions. They perform strangers convincingly. Beat: tension beneath civility.

chapters.title: What the Harbor Remembers
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He suspects his ghostwriter knows too much about a summer ten years ago and requests the sessions move to Greywater Island, where it all began. Beat: longing disguised as logistics.

chapters.title: Ferry Weather
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She arrives on Greywater against her better judgment; the island's bakery—hers once, in every way but the sign—is exactly as she left it. Beat: homecoming as wound.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The last ferry cancels; a blizzard seals the island for days. Trapped together, they negotiate rules like diplomats: no past, no names, no touching. Beat: forced intimacy, mutual armor.

chapters.title: Flour, Salt, Water
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Snowed in, he bakes out of habit and finds Mara kneading beside him at 3 a.m., hands remembering what her mouth denies. Beat: muscle memory as confession.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake of Our Twenties
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A bottle of rye loosens the story of their first meeting—the disaster wedding cake, the kiss in the walk-in. Laughter cracks the ice. Beat: warmth returning like feeling to frostbitten skin.

chapters.title: Chapter She Never Wrote
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Reading her draft notes, he finds pages about himself written with devastating tenderness—and one sentence revealing she left because of a betrayal she never named. Beat: mystery deepens into ache.

chapters.title: The Night the Power Fails
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Candlelight, cold kitchen, shared sleeping bags near the oven. They almost cross the line; Mara pulls back, shaking. Beat: desire versus self-protection.

chapters.title: What Survival Cost
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Flashback chapter: the night she discovered Elias's business partner had stolen her recipes and Elias stayed silent to save the bakery. She chose exile over erasure. Beat: the wound explained, not excused.

chapters.title: His Side of the Silence
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He confesses he knew about the theft, that silence was the price of keeping the ovens lit, and that he has hated himself for a decade. Beat: guilt met with fury, then grief.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Storm breaks; roads clear; neither mentions leaving. They cook a meal for two like it means something. Beat: fragile truce, tentative hope.

chapters.title: The Editor Calls
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Her editor demands the manuscript early and suggests cutting 'the unnamed woman' entirely—making Mara's absence permanent in print. Beat: the outside world reasserting its claims.

chapters.title: Rival Kitchens
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A rival chef arrives by ice-road taxi to poach Elias for a TV deal—and recognizes Mara, threatening to expose the ghostwriter. Beat: stakes turn public and professional.

chapters.title: Invisible No More
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Blackmailed, she nearly flees on foot across the ice; Elias finds her at the harbor edge. First real fight in ten years, all truth finally spoken. Beat: climax of conflict.

chapters.title: Forgiving the Mirror
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Alone in the bakery loft, she reads her own old journal and confronts the person she became to survive: someone who mistook invisibility for safety. Beat: internal climax, turning inward.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He offers her co-authorship and half the bakery—not charity, restitution. She doesn't answer yet. Beat: offer as atonement, patience as love.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Ferry day. She boards with the finished manuscript—her name now on the title page beside his. Beat: decision made visible.

chapters.title: Crossing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the water, they read the final chapter aloud to each other, laughing and crying as the harbor shrinks behind them. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Byline
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Publication day in the city; reviews name her. She walks past her old anonymous life without looking back. Beat: identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: A Bakery for the Harbor
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Spring reopening of the Greywater bakery, new sign, both names. The town comes; the bread is good. Beat: belonging earned.

chapters.title: Epilogue: What the Heart Learns
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. One year later, teaching a baking class, she tells students the heart is a muscle after all—it grows stronger the more you let it break open. Final image: Elias flour-dusted in the doorway. Beat: peace, earned and warm.
